{{nihongo|'''Kawaketamikabe Shrine'''|河桁御河邊神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Kawaketamikabe Shrine''' (かわけたみかべじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{読み仮名|Jinden-chō|じんでんちょう}}, {{ill|Higashiōmi|Q240891|qid=Q240891}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is a candidate for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. The shrine crest is Dakisawagata.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Yukaketa-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seoritsu-hime-no-Kami}}
* Inakura-tama-no-Mikoto

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was solicited in year 4 of {{ill|Emperor Senka|Q329728|qid=Q329728}} by local powerful clan leader Tamao Sukune Isotohiko no Muraji. It is a candidate shrine for the Engishiki {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} "Kawaketa Shrine." In ancient times it was called "Mikawabe Daimyōjin." The present shrine building is said to have been rebuilt in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 15 ({{ill|1610|ab|1610|af|1610|als|1610|am|1610 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1610|ar|1610|ary|1610|arz|1610|ast|1610|avk|1610|az|1610|azb|۱۶۱۰ (میلادی)|ban|1610|bcl|1610|be|1610|be_x_old|1610|bg|1610|bn|১৬১০|bpy|মারি ১৬১০|br|1610|bs|1610.|ca|1610|cdo|1610 nièng|ce|1610 шо|ceb|1610|ckb|١٦١٠|crh|1610|cs|1610|cv|1610|cy|1610|da|1610|de|1610|diq|1610|el|1610|eml|1610|eo|1610|es|1610|et|1610|eu|1610|fa|۱۶۱۰ (میلادی)|fi|1610|fo|1610|fr|1610|frr|1610|fur|1610|fy|1610|ga|1610|gan|1610年|gcr|1610|gd|1610|gl|1610|gv|1610|he|1610|hi|1610|hr|1610.|hsb|1610|ht|1610 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1610|hy|1610|hyw|1610 թուական|ia|1610|id|1610|ilo|1610|io|1610|is|1610|it|1610|ja|1610年|jv|1610|ka|1610|kaa|1610|kk|1610 жыл|kn|೧೬೧೦|ko|1610년|krc|1610 джыл|la|1610|lb|1610|lez|1610 йис|li|1610|lij|1610|lmo|1610|lt|1610 m.|lv|1610. gads|mai|१६१०|map_bms|1610|mdf|1610|mg|1610|mhr|1610|mi|1610|mk|1610|mr|इ.स. १६१०|mrj|1610 и|ms|1610|my|၁၆၁၀|myv|1610 ие|mzn|۱۶۱۰|nah|1610|nap|1610|nds|1610|new|सन् १६१०|nl|1610|nn|1610|no|1610|nrm|1610|nso|1610|olo|1610|or|୧୬୧୦|os|1610-æм аз|pl|1610|pnb|1610|pt|1610|qu|1610|ro|1610|ru|1610 год|rue|1610|sa|१६१०|sah|1610|scn|1610|sd|1610ع|se|1610|sh|1610.|shn|1610|simple|1610|sk|1610|sl|1610|smn|1610|sq|1610|sr|1610|stq|1610|su|1610|sv|1610|sw|1610|szl|1610|ta|1610|te|1610|tg|Соли 1610|th|พ.ศ. 2153|tk|1610|tl|1610|tly|1610|tr|1610|tt|1610 ел|ug|1610|uk|1610|ur|1610ء|uz|1610|vec|1610|vi|1610|vls|1610|wa|1610|war|1610|wuu|1610年|xmf|1610|yi|1610|zh|1610年|zh_min_nan|1610 nî|zh_yue|1610年|qid=Q6765}}) by Tanaka Yoshihisa, and a ridge tag records "Kaki Misono Mikawabe Shōichii Daimyōjin, Kanzaki District, Gōshū." In early {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was renamed to the current shrine name, and in Meiji 14 ({{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}}) was added as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

[[ファイル:Kanekai Site, gaikan.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Kanekai archaeological site}}]]
In {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 20 ({{ill|2008|Q2004|qid=Q2004}}), posthole remains believed to be an early Heian three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} honden were found at the nearby Kanekai site<ref>Shiga Prefecture cultural properties, historic sites (2012)</ref>, and one theory infers a relationship with this shrine.
